_note: Buildings you order at the start of a round. requires = another building that must be ordered first. basic = always on offer in the build phase, never drafted as a blueprint, never dealt as a building card (see build_hand_size in balance.json). workshop = craftspeople work here (slots = how many at once) on the recipes in data/recipes.json. stall = sells one kind of good (data/recipes.json) to heroes, at Fair price (price levels are a dev tuning knob only). gift = goods added to stock the moment the building stands. grudge_all = every raider a tower hits turns on it, not just sentient ones (a Wrathful roll, data/card_mods.json). tower_hp = a tower that shoots (attack, range, cooldown) can be broken: sentient raiders it hits turn on it for tower_grudge_seconds (balance.json); at 0 it stops shooting until every tower is mended to full at dawn. prize = shells paid to a hero for each kill of a creature with that tag, from the settlement's stock; yields = extra goods from those kills. work = craftsperson-seconds to raise it. fuel = extra fuel burned each night once raised (homes need heat). age = the tech age a building needs (data/ages.json). ages_up = raising it moves the town into that age. min_people = people (townsfolk and heroes) the town needs before you can order it. lodging = heroes sleep here: beds, rest (how fast energy comes back), wake_radius (how close an enemy must come to wake a sleeper), heal (HP per second while resting), night_price (shells each sleeper pays the town per night, if they have them). Any lodging lets heroes appear in dawn picks. near = where it likes to stand in the ring town (data/town.json): hearth (inner rings, the default), outer (outer rings), tended (outer rings, beside the most untended nodes it would tend), warned_side (outer rings facing this round's warned attack) gate_guard (just outside the gate with fewest guards, else over the busiest unguarded lane), a building id (beside one) or gate (a gap between two buildings of a ring that the busiest desire path runs through). daily = goods it brings in every dawn with no workers, before the town eats. paves = craftspeople pave the busiest worn paths once it stands. hearth_hp = adds to the hearth's max health once it stands. max_by_age = a higher max once the town reaches that age. worked_by = its daily goods only come while enough of that role (per building) are in town. attack/range/cooldown = it shoots at enemies in range like a watch post. tends = each dawn, every node carrying tag within radius of it regrows share of its full size (on top of node_regrow_per_day, once per such building); share 0 tends nothing until an upgrade raises it (the stone-layers' yard's Deep quarry, the hunting lodge's Game warden). craft_speed = its craftspeople work that much faster (1.0 = twice as fast; the Practised upgrades add it). copy_cost = an everyday building that can be built again (Yusuf, 2026-10-26): each one costs that share more for every one already built or ordered (0.5 = the second costs half again, the third twice). rarity = how rare its blueprint is (data/rarity.json; none = white): rarer ones are offered less often and do stranger or stronger things. effects = effect keys summed into RunState.mod() while it stands, same keys as data/relics.json, plus band_ease (bands form that many townsfolk sooner), near_wake (the nearest ring's seams count that much more when the earth picks the seam that wakes; a Wellspring, data/card_mods.json) and trophy_whims (trophy-hunting whims that many times more often). eats = goods it uses up each dawn with the town's food. prize xp = extra XP share for those kills (0.5 = half again). drills = heroes with nothing to do by day train here: xp_per_second, and energy drains energy_mult times as fast. hounds = each dawn up to heroes heroes get a hound (+attack; each eats food a dawn; lost when its hero falls back badly hurt). duels = each dawn heroes carrying tag spar in pairs: both gain xp, the loser loses hurt of their max HP. gate_hp = it is a gate: your people walk through it, raiders batter it, each of its squares has this much health, mended each dawn. assist = townsfolk with no trip worth taking lend a hand here (sim/folk_ai.gd _lend_a_hand): tribespeople only if their leaning is in leanings (or they have none), craftspeople at any workshop; hands = helpers at once (default 1). At a workshop a helper speeds what is being made at assist_rate of its work rate (balance.json); at a food building each seconds of help earns food more at the next dawn, up to food_max a day. runners = a building tagged courier sends up to slots tribespeople from the town to carry provisions from the provisions stall to heroes in the wilds (out to reach from the hearth) who called for them; heroes pay the stall price plus fee (sim/folk_ai.gd _dispatch_runners, sim/hero_ai.gd _call_for_supplies). tags staple = always in a run's blueprint pool (see blueprint_pool_share in balance.json). outpost = it stands out in the wilds by the farthest stocked node that gives gives (no plot): each dawn it takes up to take of it into stock; an enemy within raid_radius wrecks it (it needs rebuild_share of its work again); if its node is worked out it moves to the next free one and must be raised again. reckons = it keeps the town's tally (the Reeve's hut): the Your people panel and hover lines show while it stands, and townsfolk dawn cards of a Stretched role are drawn 1 + dawn_tilt times as often, a Slack one that many times less (People.reeve_tilt). plate_knobs {tag: {knob: add}} = while it stands, adds to the numbers of every near plate kind with the tag, like the relic effect (data/relics.json, Earth.kind_def).

watch_post.name: Watch post
watch_post.text: Shoots arrows at foes near it. Sentient raiders it hits may turn on it; broken, it stops shooting until mended at dawn. Each new watch post stands just outside a gate that has none yet, or over the next likely gate spot.

longhouse.name: Longhouse
longhouse.text: Hero lodging (3 beds). Plain but watchful. Heroes can appear in dawn picks.

tavern.name: Mead hall
tavern.text: Hero lodging (3 beds). Heroes rest fast and pay 2 shells a night, but sleep deeply. Greedy and brave heroes love it.

shrine.name: Spirit shrine
shrine.text: Hero lodging (2 beds). Heroes heal as they rest and wake at the first sign of danger. Cautious and dutiful heroes prefer it.

garden.name: Garden patch
garden.text: Roots and greens tended between chores: 2 food every dawn, steady whatever the gatherers find. Needs no workers, but a forager with nothing to fetch can tend it for up to 2 more.

drying_rack.name: Drying rack
drying_rack.text: Food lasts: each day's food upkeep is 25% lower.

market.name: Market square
market.text: Open ground for stalls. Heroes sell their finds here.

arms_stall.name: Arms stall
arms_stall.text: Sells the knapper's blades and spears, and later the bronzesmith's swords and axes, to heroes.

hide_stall.name: Armour stall
hide_stall.text: Sells hide armour, fur cloaks and, later, bronze scale to heroes.

charm_stall.name: Charm stall
charm_stall.text: Sells carved charms and bronze torcs to heroes.

provisions_stall.name: Provisions stall
provisions_stall.text: Sells smoked meat (energy in the field) and poultices (a heal when hurt).

knapper.name: Knapper
knapper.text: A craftsperson knaps flint blades and bone spears, and obsidian edges once heroes bring obsidian.

hide_rack.name: Hide rack
hide_rack.text: A craftsperson works beast hides into armour and cloaks.

bone_carver.name: Bone carver
bone_carver.text: A craftsperson carves bone and antler into charms.

reeves_hut.name: Reeve's hut
reeves_hut.text: An elder keeps tally sticks of who did what. Opens the Your people panel (how each kind of townsperson spent the round, by leaning) and each townsperson's day on hover, and the dawn deals more of the people the town is stretched for and fewer of those standing idle.

runners_hut.name: Runners' hut
runners_hut.text: Its runners (tribespeople from the town) carry smoked meat and poultices from the provisions stall to heroes out in the wilds who run low, so they stay out longer. Heroes pay the stall price plus a 3-shell fee; runners stop at dusk and can be caught by monsters.

smoke_hut.name: Smoke hut
smoke_hut.text: A craftsperson smokes meat and brews poultices from food and fuel.

forester.name: Forester's hut
forester.text: A forester tends the wild plants around it: each dawn, brush, groves and berry thickets within reach regrow a sixth of their size, on top of their own slow regrowth.

charcoal_pit.name: Charcoal pit
charcoal_pit.text: When fuel runs low, a craftsperson smoulders wood into charcoal for the fire: 3 wood make 6 fuel, twice what the wood gives burned raw. It stops once there is fuel for two nights.

hunting_lodge.name: Hunting lodge
hunting_lodge.text: Pays heroes 3 shells for every beast they kill, and skins each beast for 1 extra hide.

stone_yard.name: Stone-layers' yard
stone_yard.text: Craftspeople with nothing else to do pave the busiest worn paths: 1 stone for every 5 paces of stone path. Anyone on a road walks faster, raiders too.

gate.name: Gate
gate.text: Goes beside a building of a ring where the busiest path runs, best filling a gap between two. Your people walk through; raiders must batter it down or go round. Mended each dawn.

bronze_moot.name: Bronze moot
bronze_moot.text: A stone circle where the elders meet traders from the south. Raising it brings the bronze age: copper seams, the smelter, the bronzesmith, bronze tools and a southern caravan that lays out trade deals each round. The traders bring 2 bronze ingots, and it adds 30 to the hearth's health.

smelter.name: Smelter
smelter.text: A craftsperson smelts cassiterite into tin, then copper and tin into bronze ingots. Ingots go to the bronzesmith or to tool sets.

bronzesmith.name: Bronzesmith
bronzesmith.text: A craftsperson casts bronze swords, axes, scale armour and torcs for the stalls.

stone_keep.name: Stone keep
stone_keep.text: A squat stone tower where the town's first lord holds court. Raising it brings the medieval age: bog iron, charcoal and steel, townhouses and fields, families at dawn, the guildhall and the chapel. Its crossbows shoot at raiders, it adds 60 to the hearth's health, and the lord brings 3 iron.

townhouse.name: Townhouse
townhouse.text: Timber and stone: room for 6 more people, but it burns more fuel.

field.name: Field
field.text: Ploughed strips on the edge of town: 4 food every dawn while 2 tribespeople per field are free to work it (twice that with iron ploughs). Foragers with nothing to fetch can work it for up to 2 more.

charcoal_burner.name: Charcoal burner
charcoal_burner.text: A craftsperson stacks and smothers wood: 3 wood make 2 charcoal, which the bloomery and the blacksmith burn.

bloomery.name: Bloomery
bloomery.text: A craftsperson smelts bog iron with charcoal into iron blooms. Iron goes to the blacksmith or to tool sets.

blacksmith.name: Blacksmith
blacksmith.text: A craftsperson folds iron and charcoal into steel, and forges iron spears, steel longswords, mail and plate for the stalls.

guildhall.name: Guildhall
guildhall.text: Hero lodging (4 beds). Heroes pay 1 shell a night in dues. Knights only answer the call once it stands. Brave and dutiful heroes like it.

chapel.name: Chapel
chapel.text: Pays heroes 4 shells for every undead they lay to rest. A craftsperson here makes reliquaries that hit the undead harder.

gibbet_post.name: Gibbet post
gibbet_post.text: Pays heroes 2 shells for every human raider they kill, and the gibbet warns off the rest.

warden_hut.name: Barrow warden's hut
warden_hut.text: Pays heroes 3 shells for every undead they lay to rest, and the warden teaches them the old ways: half again the XP from undead kills.

trophy_hall.name: Trophy hall
trophy_hall.text: Pays heroes 6 shells for each great beast or champion they bring down (cave bears, the antlered king, hollow knights, men-at-arms, the Black Margrave), and heroes go trophy hunting three times as often.

training_yard.name: Training yard
training_yard.text: Heroes with nothing to do by day drill here: they gain XP as they train, but tire half again as fast.

kennel.name: Kennel
kennel.text: Each dawn gives a hound to up to 2 heroes, the highest level first: +3 attack while it runs with them. Each hound eats 1 food a dawn and bolts when its hero falls back badly hurt.

duel_ring.name: Duelling ring
duel_ring.text: Each dawn the bold heroes (brave and greedy) spar in pairs: both gain 8 XP, and the loser starts the day hurt.

seer_tent.name: Seer's tent
seer_tent.text: A seer reads who is coming: every dawn shows one more card to pick from.

brewhouse.name: Brewhouse
brewhouse.text: Ale brings people together: every band of like-minded tribespeople forms with 1 fewer member. Brewing eats 2 food a dawn.

levy_hall.name: Levy hall
levy_hall.text: Rule-breaker. On the warned night tribespeople take up spears from the hall: they fight raiders near the town and hit as hard as warriors. Its fire burns 1 more fuel every night.

bone_pit.name: Bone pit
bone_pit.text: Rule-breaker. Each night the first 3 foes to fall rise from the pit as skeletons that fight for the town until dawn. Keeping the dead quiet burns 2 more fuel every night.

beacon_tower.name: Beacon tower
beacon_tower.text: Rule-breaker. The beacon draws the warned attack: it always comes from one side only, but a sixth larger.

counting_house.name: Counting house
counting_house.text: Rule-breaker. Shells you hold earn 10% each round (at most 25), but traders who see your coffers leave half as many shells.

oath_stone.name: Oath stone
oath_stone.text: Rule-breaker. Heroes who swear on the stone hit 3 harder and have 15 more health at once, but learn only half as fast from their kills.

woodcutters_camp.name: Woodcutters' camp
woodcutters_camp.text: Outpost. Stands out by the farthest grove: each dawn it brings in up to 5 wood from it. Any raider or monster that comes close wrecks it until craftspeople raise it again; if the earth takes its grove, it must be raised by another.

quarry_camp.name: Quarry camp
quarry_camp.text: Outpost. Stands out by the farthest rocks: each dawn it brings in up to 4 stone from them. Any raider or monster that comes close wrecks it until craftspeople raise it again; if the earth takes its rocks, it must be raised by others.

foragers_camp.name: Foragers' camp
foragers_camp.text: Outpost. Stands out by the farthest berry thicket: each dawn it brings in up to 4 food from it. Any raider or monster that comes close wrecks it until craftspeople raise it again.

tin_diggings.name: Tin diggings
tin_diggings.text: Outpost. Stands by the farthest cassiterite vein, out by the dens: each dawn it digs up to 2 cassiterite for the smelter. Monsters roam there, so it is often wrecked and must be raised again.

causeway.name: Causeway
causeway.text: Logs laid across the wet ground: everyone crosses the Fen faster (70% of their pace becomes 90%), raiders too.

lookout_cairn.name: Lookout cairn
lookout_cairn.text: Piled stone on the town's edge: towers and the hearth see raiders a fifth farther on the Stonefield and through the Greenwood.
